ALG034 TO Q16: INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF THE PAID SOURCE BRIDGE
13 October 2026

VERDICT: ACCEPT, in the bounded mathematical scope below. No required repair.

Accept the power-of-two normalization and requantization lemma, its strict
norm boundary handling and O(m)-bit immutable-source construction, the paid
source-level conversion ledger, and the conditional same-allowance BUCKETS
consequence under the exact Delta/alpha <= rho check. The specified target
and the exact kernel/near-kernel limitations are correct.

This does not accept a production adapter, arbitrary external-input parser,
new ALG034 executable, complete Q16 recovery, bounded adaptive retry policy,
all-length transfer, full DFT algorithm, sub-FFT bound or practical speed claim.
The candidate's executable test kernel returns a list; the report expressly
requires a separately constructed immutable tuple with Q16's nested dyadic
fields. That excluded wrapper is not silently certified by this acceptance.

Priority 40 is only a supporting next-work recommendation. No score or status
in an external tracker is changed. ALG034's parent priority 48 and Q16's parent
priority 60 are unchanged. The bridge does not remove their broader open gates.

2. COMPLETE DOMAIN AND REPRESENTATION CHECKLIST

The bridge alone permits M=2^m, integer m>=2, exact signed integer Cartesian
numerators a_j,b_j, common integer exponent kappa, and integer F>=m+3. The
O(m)-bit conclusion specifically chooses F=Pq+1=16m+17. Arbitrarily larger
standalone F must remain in the resource and width account.

The ALG034 premise is the accepted specified serial fixed-point producer:
 N=M, N>=3, integer 3<=B_A<=N, 0<a<N, gcd(a,N)=1,
 integer 0<=beta_A<N, balanced contiguous blocks with longer blocks first,
 exact intended phase embedding and frequency-index output order.
For a nonzero exact input on common grid 2^-F_in, let W_in be its maximum
Cartesian numerator bit length and e=W_in-F_in. Precision p must obey
 p>=W_in and 2 C 2^-p <= 2^-t, with integer t>=0,
 C=64 H B_A 2^B_A N^2,
 H=min{binomial(N+B_A-1,B_A),2^(N-B_A)}.
The accepted sufficient formula is
 p>=max{W_in,t+B_A+ceil(log2 H)+ceil(log2 B_A)+2ceil(log2 N)+7}.
The producer's fixed-point rounding, certified phases, exact index work,
integer-range and double-width accumulator promises must all hold.
It returns Yhat=z*2^(e-p) and a bound Delta=C*2^(e-p) on the complex maximum
coordinate error from Y=U_N P_(a,beta_A)x. The exact-zero original-input branch
is separate and may return exact zero without defining W_in for zero.

The accepted Q16 BUCKETS component requires its exact WindowSpec and immutable
DyadicSource representation. Its standalone domain is dyadic M>=16, dyadic
B_Q>=4, B_Q divides M, T=M/B_Q>=4, integer r>=1 and Pq>=8, and
 W_window=2r(8B_Q-1)+1<M. These jointly imply at least M=64. Thus m>=2 in the
bridge lemma does not authorize BUCKETS calls at M=4 or M=8.
Every sample is ((real_numerator,F),(imag_numerator,F)), in an immutable
M-tuple, with exact integer fields and |numerator|<=2^F. A common F field alone
must be expanded into this accepted input representation or an independently
certified equivalent before invoking the component. Full prior validation
and strict norm >1/2 belong to the caller; BUCKETS checks only sampled cells.

The conditional published-budget consequence fixes Pq=16m+16. For the actual
E(beta_Q) sparse regime, additionally retain the rational 0<beta_Q<1/2,
 k=2^ceil(2 beta_Q m),
 B_Q=2^ceil((1/2+beta_Q)m), r=2m+1, and B_Q>=4096k,
with all the previous compactness/divisibility guards. Both rational beta
field widths must be charged. Do not identify beta_Q with beta_A, B_Q with
B_A, or Pq with p. The outer transfer's guards, including beta_Q*m>=2 and its
own t<M condition, remain outside this bridge; outer t is not the upstream
tolerance exponent. No dense fallback is added by this review.

Each call requires odd integer 1<=sigma<M and integer 0<=tau<M. Source and
target metadata, source immutability, exact types, shapes, ordering, bound
provenance and intended root sign are genuine premises. The candidate clearly
excludes a hardened deserialization/validation API. The independent wrapper
controls in this review demonstrate a possible finite domain boundary; they
do not establish that the candidate implements one.

3. NORMALIZATION AND STRICT BOUNDARY: INDEPENDENT PROOF

Let S=sum_j(a_j^2+b_j^2). If S>0, define the minimal nonnegative L with
S<=4^L. For an integer S,
 L=ceil(bit_length(S-1)/2)=((S-1).bit_length()+1)//2.
This handles S=1 and exact powers of four. Set lambda=2^(kappa+L).
Minimality proves
 1/2 < ||Yhat/lambda||_2 <=1.
No absolute power 2^kappa needs to be expanded.

Rounding each Cartesian component to the F-grid gives q/2^F with each
Cartesian component in [-1,1], because both endpoints are grid points.
The coordinate complex error is at most sqrt(2)*2^(-F-1), and the vector
error is at most sqrt(2M)*2^(-F-1)<1/4 when F>=m+3, m>=2.
The rounded vector consequently has norm strictly above 1/4.

If its squared norm is at most 1/4, double it. All its Cartesian coordinates
were then at most 1/2 in absolute value, so the doubled source still obeys
the magnitude promise, and now has norm strictly greater than 1/2. Otherwise
leave it alone. The test 4 Sq <= 2^(2F) uses equality deliberately.
Only one doubling is necessary.

Set d to 2 on the doubling branch and 1 otherwise. The correct returned scale
is alpha=2^(kappa+L-log2 d), and v=d*q/2^F. Therefore
 ||v-Yhat/alpha||_infinity <= d*sqrt(2)*2^(-F-1) <= 2^(1-F).
With F=Pq+1, this is at most rho=2^-Pq. The numerator magnitude is bounded
by 2^F, requiring at most F+1 magnitude bits plus sign. Exponent F needs only
O(log(F+2)) bits. The magnitude requirement is Cartesian; the total source
norm on the no-doubling branch need not remain at most one after rounding,
and Q16 does not require that extra restriction.

The impulse (2^K+1,0), with K>F+1, initially rounds to norm exactly 1/2.
Omitting the doubling violates the strict norm promise. Keeping lambda as
alpha after doubling instead makes the represented target wrong by roughly
1/2. Both errors are independently detected across signs, axes and precisions.

For S=0, ZERO_APPROXIMATION means only Yhat=0. A positive error radius cannot
establish Y=0. No normalized nonzero Q16 source is returned. If the original
input is independently known to be exactly zero, its exact-zero producer
branch can establish Y=0. These two kinds of zero must not be conflated.

4. THE ERROR CONSTANT, SCALE AND EXACT GUARD

The accepted BUCKETS source at its error-construction lines and the accepted
review's 'Error constants on every permitted affine pair' section give
 E=(2M^2+2W_window rho)(1+rho)^(b+1)-2M^2+rho,
where b=log2 B_Q. This is an upper certificate, not necessarily the actual
error. Its accepted simplified intermediate bound is
 E<=(16b+7)M^2 rho.
That coefficient is sharper than the published 24(m+1), but is not claimed
to be the optimal mathematical constant.

An independent short derivation confirms ample slack. Since
(b+1)rho<=1/2, the binomial/geometric comparison gives
(1+rho)^(b+1)<=1+2(b+1)rho. Substitution, W_window<M and M>=4 imply
 E<=4(b+1)M^2 rho+4M rho+rho
  <=(4b+6)M^2 rho <=(16b+7)M^2 rho.
The review uses the accepted (16b+7) bound for the claimed composition; no
improved external numerical guarantee is installed.

For the ideal operator
 (L_w u)_j=M^(-1/2) sum_t w_t u_(sigma*t+tau) omega^(-jTt),
the row norm is at most ||w||_1/sqrt(M)<=M^(3/2). The support has fewer than
M consecutive indices; odd sigma makes their addresses distinct. At j=0,
signed real tap-aligned perturbations attain the l1 row norm. The scale
M^(-1/2) is essential and is detected by the independent controls.

Applying the accepted component to v and then two triangle inequalities gives
 ||Bhat-L_w(Y/alpha)||_infinity
 <= E+M^(3/2)(Delta/alpha+rho).
The component magnitude promise is required of v, not of ideal Y/alpha.
This inequality is unconditional once the source and producer premises hold.

The sufficient target certificate is the exact comparison Delta/alpha<=rho.
On that branch,
 E+M^(3/2)(Delta/alpha+rho)
 <=(16b+9)M^2 rho <=24(m+1)M^2 rho.
There is no probabilistic success condition hidden in this error argument.
The negative certificate means that this sufficient budget is not established;
it does not prove that the actual numerical result is inaccurate.

For the actual producer scale kappa=e-p, the check simplifies exactly to
 C*d*2^-L <=2^-Pq, or C*d <=2^(L-Pq) when the exponent is nonnegative.
The absolute exponent cancels. Compare significands and exponent encodings
before shifting, so an enormous absolute exponent is never expanded. The
bound C must be tied to the correct producer/input/state/precision. Increasing
p does not create a free certificate: it changes the computed numerator data
and entails an entirely paid producer rerun. Equality at the threshold passes;
forgetting d in this check can falsely pass the doubling branch.

5. TARGET AND EXACT FAILURE CONTROLS

U denotes the same unitary negative-sign M-point DFT on both sides. Character
orthogonality proves U^2=R, (Rq)_j=q_(-j mod M). Consequently a second Fourier
stage sees U(Y/alpha)=R P_(a,beta_A)x/alpha. The Q16 bucket spectral identity
uses this reflected projected vector, with the accepted positive shift phase.
It is not automatically a source of buckets for Ux. There is no missing extra
sqrt(M) in this statement: both U factors are unitary. The BUCKETS internal
B-point FFT is unnormalized and its separate 1/sqrt(M) scale is already paid.

For N=64, B_A=3, a=1, beta_A=0, the actual partition has lengths (22,21,21)
and starts (0,22,43). Its first two block phases equal one. The supplied
rank-one block map is (Px)_(s_b+t)=conjugate(S_(b,t))*d_b. It does not include
a 1/ell_b orthogonal-projection normalization. Thus x=e_0-e_1 lies in its
kernel. For x_K=e_0-(1-2^-K)e_1, only d_0=2^-K is nonzero, so
 ||Y_K||_2^2=22*2^(-2K),
 ||x_K||_2^2=1+(1-2^-K)^2.
The signal/input squared ratio tends to zero. Input width K is paid. No
uniform positive projected-signal floor follows merely from x being nonzero.

The independent controls construct the actual phase-weighted block map in
Q[zeta]/(zeta^32+1), perform exact Fourier sums, compute exact conjugate-product
energies, and apply the transform again. They verify the full projected target,
kernel, near-kernel energies and reflection, rather than only asserting 1-1=0.

An additional immediate boundary consequence is useful. If Y=0 and the
producer certificate is sound but Yhat is nonzero, then
 alpha<=lambda<2||Yhat||_2<=2sqrt(M)Delta.
Hence Delta/alpha>1/(2sqrt(M))>rho in this precision regime. An exact-kernel
input therefore cannot pass the target budget: either the approximation is
zero, or the sufficient guard fails. This is consistent with the report's
refusal to assert a terminating adaptive retry policy. It says nothing about
realized worst-case roundoff on nonkernel inputs.

6. PAID CONSTRUCTION AND SOURCE WIDTHS

The bridge requires real dense work. With q the maximum upstream numerator
magnitude width, S has O(q+m) bits. An implementation first reads all 2M
integer fields, squares and sums them, then obtains L. A second full pass
rounds all fields and accumulates Sq. It writes the final immutable source,
performing an additional bounded pass if doubling is needed. Storing a
temporary M-cell rounded array is an alternative, with the same charged
asymptotic envelope. No arbitrary callback is accepted as a free source read.

Exact shifts depend on L and F. Since L=O(q+m), arithmetic widths are
O(q+F+m). The stated schoolbook source-level bound
 O(M(q+F+m)^2+(Dexp+log(q+F+m+2))^2)
is a conservative attainable bound, where Dexp is kappa's encoding length.
New retained source storage is O(M(F+log(F+2))) bits plus tuple/address
representation. Streamed arithmetic scratch is O(q+F+m) bits. The stated
O(M(q+F+m)+Dexp) cumulative produced-integer/allocation bound is a source-level
account for a designed implementation, not a promise about Fraction checker
storage, Python object sizes, or a physical machine's memory availability.
The scalar certificate's C,e,p encodings and construction remain charged to
the upstream planning ledger and the explicit check.

The original ALG034 full input reads, normalization, phase table, B_A^2
coefficient/seed work, NB_A recurrence, precision planning, frequency mapping,
and exact output storage remain. Requantization is indispensable because
upstream width can greatly exceed O(m). The bridge's new dense source cannot
be counted as free preexisting input storage for the combined method.

The accepted Q16 constructor still pays compact-window coefficients, all
scalar certification, B_Q/2 roots and scale construction. Each call pays its
parameter/source-width validation, W_window reads, alignments and folds,
B_Q initialization, bit reversal, B_Q*b/2 butterflies, b stages and 2B_Q final
roundings. Only actual retained preparation may be reused. Uniform costs
retain beta_Q's rational-field width h. Storage/execution and physical I/O
costs are never shifted to a purported free bridge or callback. These facts
exclude a sub-FFT or end-to-end speed claim.

7. INDEPENDENT CONTROLS AND LIMITS OF EVIDENCE

Run, from this review directory or by absolute path:
 python3 independent_checks.py

The script imports only Python standard-library modules. It recreates the
bridge using an integer-square-root scale selection and Fraction nearest-even
rounding; a separate signed integer bit-window oracle checks every coordinate.
It does not import or invoke the inspected candidate adapt function. Results
are written to results/INDEPENDENT_RESULTS.json; running it changes that receipt.
The archived initial receipt is the sealed reference.
A second independent run produced a byte-identical result receipt.

PASS: 357,683 assertions, including:
 - 6,836 nonzero vectors, exhaustive {-1,0,1}^8 and wider randomized vectors;
 - 81,232 complex coordinate comparisons and exact squared-error bounds;
 - 96 strict-boundary doubling cases across signs, axes and precisions;
 - 57,414 signed nearest-even comparisons;
 - symbolic absolute exponents of magnitude 2^200 and widths to 1,025 bits;
 - 432 exact Delta/alpha comparisons and 144 threshold pairs;
 - 2,373 checks each of the accepted intermediate constant, composed budget
   and published slack, through m=256;
 - all 2,048 odd affine pairs at M=64, with 8,192 complex bucket inequalities,
   exact row-l1 attainment and missing-scale negative controls;
 - exact cyclotomic kernel and nine near-kernel/projected-reflection cases;
 - complete explicit domain cross-checks and parameter-only beta=1/4 first
   sparse crossover m=46.

Mutations checked include omitted doubling, wrong alpha after doubling,
forgotten d in the Delta check, and missing bucket scale. Invalid-domain
controls exercise only the reviewer's independently reconstructed wrapper.

The synthetic bucket taps are signed rational fixtures, not the accepted
compact window. No actual integrated ALG034-to-Q16 execution was attempted;
no full-theorem numerical parameter instance was allocated. The universal
proof, accepted component sources and exact contracts justify the acceptance;
finite tests corroborate them rather than establish all-input statements.

8. CLASSICAL CONTENT, UNASSESSED CONTRIBUTION AND DISPOSITION

Power-of-two scaling, nearest-grid rounding, induced l1 row norms, triangle
inequalities, kernel/near-kernel reasoning and DFT reflection are classical.
The FFTW primary documentation independently reopened during this review
confirms its negative forward sign, unnormalized convention and standard
frequency ordering:
 https://www.fftw.org/fftw3_doc/The-1d-Discrete-Fourier-Transform-_0028DFT_0029.html
This documentation does not prove the bridge; the unitary reflection and
composition arguments are explicitly derived above.

Bostan and Mori's primary paper, independently reopened, explicitly separates
ring-operation and bit complexity in section 1.1:
 https://arxiv.org/html/2008.08822v1
It supplies context, not a numerical implementation or speed theorem for this
bridge. No acceptance here relies on the inaccessible Higham chapter cited by
the candidate, and no claim is made to have read that chapter's full text.

The candidate-specific contribution is the contract-bound, paid connection
between the two accepted components, including the strict rounding boundary,
the exact sufficient guard and preservation of the existing bucket allowance.
Its worldwide originality remains unassessed; this is not a novelty search.
Marker ranks, CRT support minima and their finite-field results are not
silently converted into numerical conditioning statements. In particular,
actual N=16/B_A=8 balanced starts are even residues and are periodic, outside
the cited aperiodic CRT minimization domain.

FINAL: ACCEPT this scoped mathematical bridge and conditional BUCKETS budget.
No required report or theorem repair. Production-wrapper work, successful
nonkernel precision policy, correct end target, full recovery, outer transfer
and end-to-end resource claims remain open. No Sheet, GitHub, public publishing,
sharing-permission or parent-score changes were made.
